analysis.title: Whirlpool Corp. (WHR) 3Q26 Recap: Initiatives to Support Margins and Cash Flow in Focus as Visibility to Demand Further Declines
key_insights: GS keeps Neutral on WHR and cuts the 12-month price target to $35 from $41, based on 7.2x (unchanged) Q5-Q8 EBITDA. Price is $26.45, implying 32.3% upside.

GS argues rising operating pressures are largely reflected in the valuation and buyside expectations. A modest macro improvement, led by lower rates and energy prices, could lift the stock and cause a short squeeze.
2026 adj. EPS estimate cut to ($1.35) from $1.70, 2027 to $1.10 from $2.95, and 2028 to $3.10 from $4.25.

Consumers are delaying appliance purchases, including replacement units, which lowers North America volumes and mix. MDA demand weakness continued into October in line with housing and the broader macro.

Pricing continues: retail price is up high-single digits vs January 2025, with an additional 7% US increase effective early December that benefits 2027. The builder channel also took pricing in late 3Q.

GS models 2026 North America MDA revenue down 5%, with volumes down 5% and flat price/mix. Small domestic appliances (SDA) grow at a double-digit rate on global sell-out, share gains and licensing and accessory sales, and GS models segment sales up 9.7%.

Latin America: GS forecasts 2026 revenue growth of 6.6% on price realization, FX and industry sales. An increase of up to 10% comes through in coming quarters. The Casas Bahia bankruptcy shifted some volumes and hurt mix and margin. 2027 segment revenue is modeled up 1.3%.
GS models 2026 consolidated sales down 2.4% vs the company's -1.5% guide, then 3.4% growth in 2027.

Inflation in raw materials rose faster than expected, across fuel and logistics plus Section 232 tariff pressure. Steel contracts are at the higher end of the range with spot prices up 50+% in the last year. Two of three long-term steel contracts were renewed in 3Q at what management called fair prices. Steel costs are expected flat sequentially in 4Q and into early 2027.
Cost actions are on track to deliver $290mn in savings in 2027, with $230mn from structural manufacturing changes and the balance from logistics, on top of ongoing productivity efforts.
GS forecasts 2026 North America MDA adj. EBIT margin at 2.1% (4Q at 2.5%), recovering to 4.0% in 2027. SDA 4Q adj. EBIT margin is modeled at 13.8% and 15.9% for the full year.
GS models 2026 consolidated EBIT margin at 2.0%, down 269bps YoY and within the company's 2.0-2.2% guide.

Trade and company inventories are lean, which GS sees as upside to utilization if demand improves. Management detailed the 4Q free cash flow guide and reiterated confidence in liquidity after pushing maturities to 2028, securing the ABL and improving working capital.
GS channel checks show greater discipline in the length and magnitude of promotions. Market share is stable while management invests in new products.
GS scenario analysis: upside case $40 (16.5x 2027 adj. EPS) and downside case $20 (80.0x 2027 adj. EPS), which GS calls balanced risk/reward.

market_movers.rationale: GS cuts the target to $41 from $35 basis reversed: target lowered to $35 from $41 on lower estimates, keeping Neutral. Upside case $40, downside case $20.

earnings_insights: WHR 3Q26 recap (reported 10/27/2026 per the GS note): GS 2026 adj. EPS estimate ($1.35) vs prior GS estimate $1.70. GS estimate, not a reported figure.
GS 2027 adj. EPS estimate $1.10 (prior $2.95) and 2028 $3.10 (prior $4.25). All are GS estimates.
GS 2026 consolidated sales estimate down 2.4% vs company guide of -1.5%. GS consolidated EBIT margin estimate 2.0% vs company guide of 2.0-2.2%.
GS 2026E revenue $14,348.9mn (prior $14,763.6mn), EBITDA $671.3mn, FCF $194.7mn. All are GS estimates.
Company guide includes about +25bps of consolidated price/mix for 2026.
risk_factors: Upside risks to Neutral: North America MDA price/mix beats expectations, trade-action benefits exceed expectations, cost reductions deliver higher profitability, housing recovery drives R&R demand, and dividends and shareholder returns resume from debt reduction.

Downside risks: rising competition limits pricing power and raises promotions, new products fail to gain traction, raw material inflation exceeds expectations with inability to pass through costs, and trade actions increase promotions and pressure revenue and margins.
Leverage: GS estimates net debt/EBITDA of 6.7x in 2026E and interest cover of 0.2x.
vol_and_positioning: GS says the bar for buyside expectations has been lowered after the quarter and a modest macro improvement could cause a short squeeze in WHR.
geopolitical: Section 232 tariffs add incremental raw material cost pressure for WHR.
GS cites benefits from announced trade actions as an upside risk and trade actions increasing promotions as a downside risk.

tension_points.bull_case: Operating pressure is reflected in the valuation and buyside expectations, inventories are lean, pricing and $290mn of 2027 savings are on track, and a modest macro improvement could trigger a short squeeze with an upside case of $40.
tension_points.bear_case: Consumers are delaying purchases and trading down, North America MDA volumes fall 5% in 2026, raw material inflation is higher than expected, and the downside case is $20.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Raw material inflation exceeding expectations with inability to pass through costs, or rising competition limiting pricing power, would break the bull case.

theme_stances.key_argument: Pricing, lean inventories, $290mn of 2027 cost savings and working capital discipline support margins and cash flow, but demand visibility is declining.
